bullets.title: AMZN: Morgan Stanley raises PT to $350, adds as Top Pick on AWS growth outlook
bullets.body: MS analyst Brian Nowak raises AMZN PT to $350 (from $335) and adds as a Top Pick with Overweight rating, implying ~33% upside. MS raises 2027/28 AWS growth forecasts to +47%/+42%, targeting $16.56 2028 EPS, with AWS generating $164.5B of 2028 EBIT (67% of company total). CEO Jassy reportedly told Ben Horowitz AWS is sold out of compute past 2028.

bullets.title: META: MS raises PT to $820; Muse compute demand massive but engagement data mixed
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raises META PT to $820 (from $775), modeling ~13GW incremental GPU capacity in 2027-28 as every 100M Muse DAUs requires 1-4GW. However, Hedgeye/Citi note Meta AI Muse lost 42% of US weekly users within three weeks of launch, and monetization model remains unclear. Street models ~$194B of Meta 2027 capex with potential equity/debt raise post-earnings flagged as a risk.

bullets.title: MSFT: Azure expected +47% y/y; Nscale UK deal pulled on power constraints, not demand
bullets.body: Citi clarifies MSFT pulled out of Nscale U.K. datacenter deal due to power grid constraints, explicitly not a demand issue. MS models ~4.25GW incremental capacity in FY27 with FY27 capex expected above $220B; custom silicon Maia 300 enters production at multi-GW scale in 2027. MSFT may discontinue disclosing Copilot seat additions (currently 30M+ paid seats).

bullets.title: CRWV: Goldman upgrades to Buy ($106 PT); debt concerns persist with ~16% bond yield
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs upgraded CRWV to Buy from Neutral with a $106 PT (down from $139), sending the stock +6.9% pre-market. However, Citi and 22V flag CRWV unsecured bonds trading at ~16% yield with CDS spreads near 1,000 bps, with only a 2-3 year runway to exit the debt cycle given heavy OpenAI exposure. Hedgeye maintains CRWV as an active short.

bullets.title: APP: Citi cuts PT to $500 (from $600) on mobile game deceleration, execution risk
bullets.body: Citi reduces APP's 3Q preview PT from $600 to $500, lowering the valuation multiple from 29x to 25x 2027 FCF, citing sharper mobile games deceleration and elevated execution risk following the 2Q26 miss. Hedgeye's signal model has APP as a top short, while Citi still expects a modest 3Q beat on seasonality and model enhancement. AppLovin trades near a five-year multiple low per Hedgeye comms.

bullets.title: NFLX: Film chief Dan Lin dismissed ahead of Tuesday earnings; options imply ~8.9% move
bullets.body: Netflix dismissed head of film Dan Lin over the weekend, following ~1K layoffs including CCO Bela Bajaria; Peter Rice (ex-Disney TV chairman) named new CCO effective Oct 26. Q3 earnings are due Oct 20 after close with revenue consensus $12.87B vs. guidance $12.86B and EPS $0.82 vs. guidance $0.82. Hedgeye notes Netflix global Top-10 viewing hours fell 11% in Q3 and TV viewing share down 1pt YoY as key headwinds.

bullets.title: RBLX: Citi Buy maintained; Week 42 CCUs up 4% sequentially, consistent with $2.08B 4Q26 bookings
bullets.body: Citi reiterates Buy on Roblox; Week 42 average peak CCUs of 15.9M are down 15% YoY but up 4% sequentially, consistent with 4Q26 bookings of $2.08B. Hedgeye flags Q3 bookings were guided down 14-18% with the October 29 guide critical for valuation; JPM also highlights Roblox trend durability as a key debate into 3Q earnings.

bullets.title: DKNG: PA data strong (+29% GGR), NFL Week 6 favorable hold, Wells Fargo sees stocks oversold
bullets.body: Pennsylvania September data shows DKNG sports betting GGR +29% YoY with 32% handle share (up from 30%), while FanDuel GGR fell -17%. NFL Week 6 estimated industry hold of 10-12% with big upsets favoring books; DKNG specifically expected to benefit from low TD scoring and unfavorable public betting outcomes. Wells Fargo views DKNG as oversold with CAC spend expected to prove temporary, and Citi notes recent long-only demand returning on dips.

bullets.title: INTC: Upgraded to Neutral at JPMorgan (from Underweight); $85 PT unchanged
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgrades INTC to Neutral from Underweight with target $85 unchanged; stock traded +4.6% pre-market. Wolfe's chip team flags INTC achieves $8-10 EPS power in CY29-30 across most scenarios but execution risk and limited certainty vs. alternatives with similar AI exposure and multiples argues against a thesis change.

bullets.title: MRVL: UBS views MSFT Maia as key upside driver; Vera Rubin delays immaterial to revenue
bullets.body: UBS is bullish on the analog semiconductor setup into earnings and specifically identifies Microsoft's Maia custom silicon as a key source of upside for Marvell. Minor delays in Vera Rubin ramp are noted as having no effect on revenue recognition.

bullets.title: SHOP: JPM Top Pick for Internet SMid; AI/agentic commerce (Sidekick & Muse) key debate
bullets.body: JPM names SHOP as a top pick for Internet SMid heading into 3Q earnings, with an expert call hosted today with Shopify Platinum Partner Zettler Digital (400+ e-commerce brands) focused on AI-commerce strategy including Sidekick and Muse, enterprise adoption, and Merchant Solutions trends. SHOP traded +1.7% on the Toronto exchange Monday morning.

bullets.title: ACN: UBS Buy ($278 PT); Gemini AI monetization accelerating, China ops sale ($1.5B) eyed
bullets.body: UBS maintains Buy on ACN with $278 PT; Gemini Launchpads deployment reinforces AI monetization thesis with top 18 Alliances now representing ~65% of revenue. ACN is exploring sale of China/HK/Taiwan operations for up to $1.5B, which could fund its $8B FY27 M&A spend target and drive 2-2.5% inorganic revenue growth. Federal business expected to flip from 2026 headwind to FY27 tailwind.

bullets.title: DELL/HPE: Morgan Stanley sees on-prem hardware repatriation benefiting both on open-weight model deployments
bullets.body: MS CIO survey shows enterprises deploying open-weight AI models on proprietary on-prem hardware for security and control, driving a 'repatriation' trend away from cloud-only deployments. Both DELL and HPE are positioned to benefit; DELL CEO additionally flagged the memory crunch worsening in 2027 as potentially a four-year problem.

bullets.title: MU: CXMT 4F² DRAM announcement triggers selloff; mass-production viability unverified
bullets.body: Chinese memory maker CXMT announced plans to commercialize 4F² DRAM within the year, triggering selloffs in Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron on Chinese supply concerns. Mass-production viability remains unverified, leaving the ultimate competitive impact uncertain. Separately, Micron indicates memory supply constraints could intensify through 2028 per JPMorgan's TMT preview.

bullets.title: RDDT: US DAU growth decelerating to ~1% YoY; web traffic slowest growth in 21 months
bullets.body: Jefferies flags Reddit US web DAU growth down to ~1% YoY, a significant deceleration, while worldwide web traffic grew only 4.1% in September—the slowest in the 21-month tracking series. Advertising and monetization trends remain strong, but data-licensing renewals are flagged as the key upcoming catalyst. Google AI Overviews now linking to Reddit content ahead of forum results.

bullets.title: PINS: Initiated at Buy ($30 PT) by Phillip Securities; US daily users +20% but ad spend down 5%
bullets.body: Phillip Securities initiated Pinterest at Buy with a $30 PT. Hedgeye comms data shows US daily users up ~20% but agency ad spend benchmark down 5%, creating a monetization gap that is a key debate for the stock heading into earnings.

bullets.title: TSLA: Earnings Wednesday; Cybercab Austin deployments and FSD v15 progress are investor focus
bullets.body: TSLA reports Wednesday with investors focused on Cybercab deployments in Austin (live since Oct 1), FSD v15 progress, and autonomous vehicle competitive positioning. OPCO expects TSLA to push aggressively on capex for vertical integration and show improving margins on strong EV sales; Optimus ramp expectations are muted given AI training and competitive complexity.

bullets.title: APP eCommerce tracker: US store growth accelerating to 3.3% weekly in 4Q26 QTD vs. 1.5% in 3Q26
bullets.body: Citi's weekly AppLovin Ads tracker shows 18,450 global eCommerce clients as of Oct 16 (+11.5% WoW), with US stores at 6,472 (+2.7% WoW). US weekly store growth has accelerated from a 1.5% average in 3Q26 to 3.3% in 4Q26 QTD, with the most recent week hitting 3.9%—the fastest in four months. Citi maintains Buy.

bullets.title: HIMS: Mixed Q3 signals—app downloads declining QoQ while web traffic remains strong
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley SMID daily notes HIMS shows mixed Q3 data with app downloads declining quarter-over-quarter while web traffic remains strong. JPM's Internet SMid preview also lists HIMS as a focus stock into 3Q earnings alongside SHOP, APP, and RBLX.

bullets.title: HUT: Roth initiates with $108 PT; margin-of-safety value $67 from executed datacenter leases
bullets.body: Roth initiates HUT with a $108 core PT and identifies a $67 margin-of-safety value ($63/share from three executed leases + ABTC stake ~$2 + net cash ~$5 less maintenance SG&A ~$3). The $108 PT incorporates Batavia, River Bend Expansion, and ~1.9GW exclusivity pipeline. Roth flags some datacenter projects 'going dark' and q/q backlog declines as risks across the broader sector.
